name: stri_subset<-
title: Select Elements that Match a Given Pattern

origin.description: Replace the strings selected by exactly one search engine.
origin.usage: stri_subset(str, ..., regex, fixed, coll, charclass) <- value

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector to modify. The result has this length.

arguments.name: regex, fixed, coll, charclass
arguments.text: Exactly one pattern argument. A missing argument is not NULL. NULL is an empty pattern vector.
negate and the settings of the chosen search engine.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Non-empty character vector written onto the matches, in order.

origin.details: The replacement calls stri_subset_regex<-, stri_subset_fixed<-, stri_subset_coll<-, or stri_subset_charclass<-. The function returns the modified vector. A call of the function does not change the object that was passed in. The <- form assigns that vector back.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as str.
origin.example:
x <- `stri_subset<-`(c("ab", "12"), regex = "[0-9]", value = "N")
sentence <- paste0('`stri_subset<-`(c("ab", "12"), regex="[0-9]", value="N") returns ', paste(x, collapse = ", "), '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Replace the strings selected by exactly one search engine.
translation.usage: stri_subset_assign(str, *, value, regex, fixed, coll, charclass, **kwargs)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, number, logical, or list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: regex, fixed, coll, charclass
arguments.text: Exactly one pattern. Omitting the argument is not the same as None. None is an empty pattern vector.

arguments.name: kwargs
arguments.text: negate and the settings of the chosen search engine.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Replacement strings written onto the matches, in order. A missing value stays missing.

translation.details: The call goes to stri_subset_regex_assign, stri_subset_fixed_assign, stri_subset_coll_assign, or stri_subset_charclass_assign. Those functions call the translated subset search. The result is a new list. The list passed as str is not modified.
translation.value: A list the same length as str.
translation.example:
from stringi.subset import stri_subset_assign
x = stri_subset_assign(["ab", "12"], regex="[0-9]", value="N")
print('`stri_subset<-`(["ab", "12"], regex="[0-9]", value="N") returns ' + ", ".join(x) + ".")
